patches.source: the fill unit, cut with the 1881 shore
patches.note: land today that the geologic map calls fill and the 1881 Government Survey map shows as sea or reef flat: Sand Island (but for Quarantine Island), the reef under the piers of the inner harbour and Kapālama, Kakaʻako makai and the Kewalo waterfront, Ala Moana and Magic Island, and the made ground at Kālia by the Ala Wai boat harbour. Fill the 1881 map shows as land (the Kewalo ponds and Kakaʻako salt pans, the Waikīkī wetland under the Ala Wai, the Kalihi and Moanalua ponds) stays land. The 1881 shore is the earliest surveyed; at the harbour front it already includes made ground of unknown date

sources.title: USGS 3D Elevation Program lidar HI_NOAAMauiOahu_2020_B20, bare-earth DEM at its original 0.5 m, 500 m GeoTIFF tiles (NAD83(PA11) / UTM zone 4N)
sources.licence: public domain (U.S. Geological Survey, 3D Elevation Program); collected for NOAA
sources.note: 564 tiles (USGS_OPR_HI_NOAAMauiOahu_2020_B20_4QFJ140560 … USGS_OPR_HI_NOAAMauiOahu_2020_B20_4QFJ265645, part HI_NOAAMauiOahu_2_B20); every 0.5 m cell counts toward the texel its centre falls in. The survey's zero is 0.72 m below mean sea level (measured against the CUDEM on flat ground; residual 0.00 m) and is moved to it. A cell is land above +0.2 m, because water inside the coast is flattened to the level of the day it was flown (−0.35 to +0.1 m); a texel is land when at least half its cells are, and holds their mean (never below 0.25 m). 112 of the 676 squares over the box have no tile: open sea, and the windward face of the pali (see the CUDEM)

sources.title: NOAA NCEI Continuously Updated DEM (CUDEM), 1/9 arc-second topobathymetric tiles, Hawaiʻi (Digital Coast 9428), WGS 84, mean sea level
sources.licence: public domain (NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information); cite Amante, C.J., Love, M., Carignan, K., Sutherland, M.G., MacFerrin, M. and Lim, E. (2023), Continuously Updated Digital Elevation Models (CUDEMs) to Support Coastal Inundation Modeling, Remote Sensing 15(6), 1702, doi:10.3390/rs15061702
sources.note: tile ncei19_n21x50_w158x00_2021v1, about 3 m cells. Sea texels: the area-weighted mean of the cells below mean sea level, never shallower than -1 m (628553 texels; the reef flats from topobathymetric lidar, the harbour and channels from NOAA surveys); 6386 texels of water inside the coast that the CUDEM holds as land (the Ala Wai, the tidal reaches of the streams, lagoons) are a flat -1 m. Land: 239839 texels (5.8% of the pack) on the windward face of the pali, where the lidar has no tile, are the CUDEM's land there (the 2013 NOAA Oʻahu lidar on the lower slopes, the USGS 1/3 arc-second DEM on the cliffs, per its spatial metadata) plus a smooth correction that meets the lidar along the seam (seam difference median -0.8 m)
